hook.description: Opens on a title card overlay 'Episode 31 / COLLATERAL DAMAGE' laid over the kitchen scene. The wife, calmly sipping tea, deadpans 'I don't bottle things up' while beside her the husband (rendered with a black battery-shaped torso/head, the show's stylized 'low battery' character design) is silently, aggressively slamming a cabinet shut.
hook.why_it_works: The line is immediately contradicted by the visual gag right next to it -- calm words paired with a husband slamming cabinets -- so the mismatch between what's said and what's shown creates instant curiosity about the couple's actual conflict, all within the first two seconds.

setup.description: A brief dialogue-free beat: the husband keeps closing/slamming a cabinet with restrained fury (stiff posture, blank grimace, glasses askew) while the wife continues serenely handling her teacup. Word-by-word captions begin appearing (e.g. 'YOU'VE') as the wife starts to speak, priming the accusation that follows.

conflict.description: The wife calmly states the actual grievance: 'You've been closing every cabinet in this house with exactly 1% two more four since Thursday.' The husband keeps performing the same small aggressive cabinet-closing action as she talks, and a '%' icon appears onscreen -- tying his repressed anger to the show's running 'low battery' conceit, where his frustration is measured like a draining battery percentage.

punchline.description: The wife shrugs off any responsibility with the deadpan line 'I don't know what I did Thursday, but the cabinets are paying for it' -- the joke lands on the idea that neither spouse addresses the real issue, and the actual damage (the episode's title, 'Collateral Damage') is being taken out on the furniture instead.

ending.description: The scene holds briefly on the kitchen tableau after the punchline, then cuts to a black outro card reading 'LOW BATTERY PEOPLE / CREATED BY NIN.' with a yellow 'NEW EPISODE DAILY' ticket-style graphic.
ending.cta_or_text_overlay: LOW BATTERY PEOPLE -- CREATED BY NIN. -- NEW EPISODE DAILY

beat_map.description: Title card 'Episode 31 / Collateral Damage' over the scene; wife says 'I don't bottle things up' while husband silently slams a cabinet beside her.
Silent beat of the husband continuing to slam the cabinet with restrained anger as the wife sips tea; captions begin ('YOU'VE') leading into her accusation.

Wife accuses him: 'You've been closing every cabinet in this house with exactly 1% two more four since Thursday,' a '%' icon appears onscreen linking his behavior to the show's low-battery/rage-meter premise.
Wife's deadpan punchline: 'I don't know what I did Thursday, but the cabinets are paying for it,' displacing the real conflict onto the furniture.
Brief hold on the kitchen scene, then cut to black outro card with series branding 'LOW BATTERY PEOPLE, CREATED BY NIN.' and 'NEW EPISODE DAILY' ticket graphic.

narrative_notes: This is a recurring-series episode (Episode 31 of 'Low Battery People'), so the hook leans on the show's established premise (a character design where repressed anger is visualized as a draining battery) rather than explaining it from scratch -- returning viewers get the joke about '1%... since Thursday' immediately, while new viewers get it retroactively via the title card. Setup and conflict are nearly fused: setup is only a ~1.5s dialogue-free beat of the husband's cabinet-slamming before the wife's single accusatory line does double duty as both scene-setting and rising conflict. There is no separate 'reveal' or reaction shot distinct from the ending; the ending beat combines a brief hold on the punchline's aftermath with the studio's outro card in one continuous segment.
